sections.html:
Lauderdale County's seat, Meridian, lies in east central Mississippi roughly 93 miles east of Jackson and 154 miles southwest of Birmingham. A 2020 head count of 35,052 makes it the eighth largest city in the state. Interstates 20 and 59 meet here, and Amtrak's Crescent stops at Union Station on Front Street.

Rolling ground and small creeks define the terrain. Sowashee Creek crosses the southern part of town, fed by Gallagher's Creek, and Loper's Creek runs along the far west. If your lot is near one of them, look at drainage before a buyer's inspector does.

With 13.6 percent of units empty, a house in poor shape can end up competing with a lot of other vacant homes. That is one reason owners of inherited, tenant-occupied or storm-damaged houses sometimes choose a quick as-is sale over carrying taxes and insurance.

Meridian's railroad boom left nine historic districts on the National Register of Historic Places, among them East End, Highlands, Merrehope, Mid-Town, Poplar Springs Road, West End and the downtown areas around Union Station. Wealth from the Golden Age, roughly 1880 to 1910, built houses in Queen Anne, Colonial Revival, Italianate and bungalow styles. The Meridian Historic Districts and Landmarks Commission was created in 1979 to protect that character.

If your house is in or near a district, ask city planning before changing windows, siding or rooflines. A buyer will want to know whether past work was approved.

Age cuts both ways. A 1920s house has character that appeals to a retail buyer, but it can also hide knob-and-tube wiring, galvanized plumbing and a failing foundation pier. Those repairs scare off buyers who depend on a mortgage, and they explain why owners of older homes consider selling as is.

A railroad line still runs through downtown, and Meridian Regional Airport at Key Field sits about 3 miles southwest of the city. Buyers sometimes ask how close a house is to the tracks or the flight path, so know the answer for your street before you list.

Jobs also shape how fast some owners need to sell. Health care and the military base at Naval Air Station Meridian and Key Field employ thousands of people, and a transfer can come with little notice. When a move date is fixed, waiting on a buyer's loan approval is risky. A cash sale can be scheduled around your date instead.

sections.h2: Code enforcement for vacant or run-down houses
sections.html:
The Code Enforcement Division works through four code officials spread across the wards. Violations it handles include abandoned or deteriorated structures, rubbish, inoperable vehicles, overgrown grass and weeds, appliances stored outdoors and fallen fences.

The city follows a set sequence: inspect, send a notice of violation if one is found, then reinspect after a reasonable time. A property still out of compliance gets a citation and an environmental court date, and fines or liens can follow.

Any lien will surface when the buyer's title search runs. Under Mississippi Code section 21-19-11, a municipality may also declare a property a menace and charge cleanup costs to the owner as an assessment against the land. If you inherited a Meridian house you have not seen in months, drive by and look for notices posted on it. The code enforcement office is at 601-485-1998.

Lauderdale County sends the bill in November or December, payable by February 1 after the January 1 assessment. Questions go to the tax collector at 601-482-9895. A Meridian house carries a county rate, a school district rate and a city rate.

The state taxes a home that its owner lives in on 10 percent of value, and everything else on 15 percent. Real property gets a fresh valuation every four years at most, with no requirement that assessors come inside.

Think the valuation is wrong? Start with the chancery clerk and request a Board of Supervisors hearing, which usually has to happen by the first Monday in August.

Penalties and interest build on an unpaid bill. After enough time the parcel can be offered at the county tax sale, which falls on the first Monday in April or the last Monday in August depending on the county. If nobody buys it, the State of Mississippi takes it and the Secretary of State manages it. Get the exact balance from the tax collector and let the title company pay it from your proceeds.

sections.h2: If you inherited a Meridian house
sections.html: Start with the basics. Find out who holds legal title, whether taxes are current, and whether the city has posted any notice on the property. The code enforcement page links to the Secretary of State's list of tax-forfeited lands and to a neighborhood lot program, and both show how vacant lots change hands in Meridian, which is the outcome you want to avoid for a house that is still yours. Then decide how fast you need to sell. A house you cannot visit often is easiest to sell before notices, weeds and overdue bills pile up.

sections.h2: Your options for selling in Meridian
sections.html:
Three paths are open: an agent, a sale on your own, or a cash buyer. A solid house in a steady neighborhood usually does best listed. Going alone avoids the commission while leaving the form, contract and closing logistics with you.

Section 89-1-503 of the Mississippi Code makes the seller deliver a written property condition disclosure statement ahead of the title transfer. Even a cash buyer wants honest answers about the roof, plumbing, termite history and flooding. Severe spring thunderstorms can bring damaging wind, hail and tornadoes, so buyers look hard at roofs.

We can look at your address and explain a no-obligation cash offer. A cash buyer will usually take a house that needs major repairs as is, as long as you disclose known defects and clear any code liens or back taxes before closing.

After you accept an offer, a title search is ordered to turn up liens, unpaid taxes and any recorded code assessments. Whatever is owed comes out of your proceeds, then you sign the deed and the sale is recorded. A cash sale skips the lender's appraisal, so this stretch is usually short. Have your tax bill, any city notices you received and records of repairs on hand. If an older house has had work done in a historic district, bring whatever approvals you have.

faqs.a: About 35,052 people lived in Meridian in 2020, across roughly 54.5 square miles. It is the seat of Lauderdale County.

faqs.q: When are Lauderdale County property taxes due?
faqs.a: By February 1 of the year after the January 1 assessment. The tax collector's property tax line is 601-482-9895, and online payment is available through the county's payment link.

faqs.q: Do Meridian's historic districts affect my house?
faqs.a: They can. The city has nine historic districts on the National Register of Historic Places and a commission created in 1979. Check with city planning before exterior changes in or near a district.

faqs.q: What happens if my Meridian house has a code violation?
faqs.a: The city inspects, issues a notice of violation, and reinspects after a reasonable time. If the problem persists, a citation is issued and an environmental court date is set. Fines or liens may result.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Meridian house that needs major repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer will usually take it as is. Disclose known defects, and clear any code liens or back taxes before closing.
